name: Operating System
description: The complete GATE CS Operating System unit in 11 topics. Every topic has a hand-picked Hinglish lecture track and an English one, each with a transcript, AI study notes and a lecture tutor.
syllabus: System calls, processes, threads, inter-process communication, concurrency and synchronization. Deadlock. CPU and I/O scheduling. Memory management and virtual memory. File systems.

topics.title: OS Basics & System Calls
topics.summary: What an operating system does, the kinds of OS, user vs kernel mode, and how programs ask the kernel for services through system calls (including fork()).

topics.title: Processes
topics.summary: The process abstraction: states and transitions, the PCB, context switching and the schedulers that move processes between queues.

topics.title: Threads
topics.summary: Lightweight execution units inside a process: user- vs kernel-level threads and the multithreading models.

topics.title: Inter-Process Communication
topics.summary: How cooperating processes exchange data: shared memory, message passing and pipes.

topics.title: Concurrency & Synchronization
topics.summary: Race conditions and the critical-section problem, from software solutions (Peterson) to hardware locks, semaphores, monitors and the classic problems.

topics.title: Deadlock
topics.summary: When processes wait on each other forever: the four conditions, resource-allocation graphs, prevention, avoidance (Banker's algorithm), detection and recovery.

topics.title: CPU Scheduling
topics.summary: Choosing which ready process runs next: FCFS, SJF/SRTF, priority, Round Robin and multilevel queues, with Gantt-chart numericals.

topics.title: I/O & Disk Scheduling
topics.summary: Disk structure and access time, and the algorithms that order disk requests: FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK, C-LOOK.

topics.title: Memory Management
topics.summary: Allocating main memory: partitions and fragmentation, paging with page tables and TLBs, multilevel paging and segmentation.

topics.title: Virtual Memory
topics.summary: Running programs larger than memory: demand paging, page faults, page-replacement algorithms, Belady's anomaly and thrashing.

topics.title: File Systems
topics.summary: How files are stored on disk: directory structures, allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed, inode) and free-space management.
